title: What do you think about using AI for game sprites like this?
author: hodorok
selftext:
I’m a solo dev working on a top-down zombie shooter, and I’ve been experimenting with this pipeline:

ChatGPT concept → Meshy 3D model + rig → Blender animation → top-down render → Construct 3 sprite.

There’s still a lot of manual work involved, especially animation and getting everything game-ready, but it saves me a huge amount of time compared to creating every asset from scratch.

I’m curious how other indie devs feel about workflows like this.

comments.author: Ok-Beyond244
comments.body: Reminds me of an old game called Alien Shooter.

replies.author: hodorok
replies.body: Alien Shooter and Crimsonland are the main inspirations for the game. It’s just about shooting zombies / mutants.

replies.author: Ok-Beyond244
replies.body: That's crazy I've never met anyone who's played alien shooter let alone liked it so much they tried to make a game version of it. If you need any help with the project let me know.

replies.author: hodorok
replies.body:
Oh I loved that game back in the day. But this will be more like Crimsonland in gameplay sense.  
Thank you very much for the offer.  
I'm working on an observation mode of the arena without the player to test the Npc and zombies behavior. It will be ready in a few days hopefully.  
If you're interested I would love to have some feedback when it's ready.

replies.author: Ok-Beyond244
replies.body: Sure, I would love to play it and give you feedback

replies.author: hodorok
replies.body:
Hello again,  
You can see the Observation mode here:  
[http://zombieoutbreakarena.com/](http://zombieoutbreakarena.com/)

This doesn't include the player. So it is not a playable demo. Just observing the active arena.  
  
I wanted to check the zombies versus Npcs and different Npc teams and hostility between them.  
Also the physics obstacles, destructible objects and recycle of objects.  
You can see the drones brining the new objects and collecting the destroyed vehicles etc.  
  
I have 2 player controls ready with shared screen but I'm not ready to share a playable demo soon. I want to construct the functioning arena before that.

So basically this is for me to watch and refine weapons, npcs and zombies.

You can change some settings with sliders. Also enable / disable auto cam follow / zoom.

I would appreciate if you could let me know the fps at the bottom of the screen when there is a lot of zombies and npcs around.

PS. It should also work on mobile. Can move the screen with drag and zoom with pinch.

comments.author: gcampos
comments.body:
Nobody here is going to tell you to not use AI, but the suggestion I would give to you is to think what you can do to add your own style in the generated art, otherwise looks too generic.

I havent used much AI for asset creation, but I used it a lot for text. I created a [VOICE.md](http://VOICE.md) which was a set of rules to make sure the "voice" of the text was what I wanted.

replies.author: hodorok
replies.body:
Thank you.  
Actually I'm aiming for generic graphics until I finish developing the game mechanics. After everything is working I can always remake the graphics. But this is making the development process incredibly fast. Also using ChatGPT codex to help with complex Construct 3 events, made everything 10 times faster.
